newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Gencor leaves Zambia Konkola copper.
newsitem.headline: Gencor leaves Zambia Konkola copper.

text.p: South African mining house Gencor Ltd announced on Thursday that it has withdrawn from a consortium interested in developing Zambia's Konkola Deep copper project.
"Gencor has withdrawn from a consortium which is conducting a feasibility study and negotiations on the (Konkola project)," Gencor said in a statement.
The consortium comprises Anglo American Corp of South Africa subsidiary Zambia Copper Investments Ltd (ZCI) (40 percent), Gencor Ltd (30 percent) and Falconbridge Ltd (30 percent).
"After careful study, Gencor concluded that in view of all the current circumstances the project would probably not meet its investment criteria," Gencor said.

Anglo's ZCI said in a statement that it and Falconbridge would continue with the feasibility study and ongoing negotiations with the Zambian government and Zambia Consolidated Copper Mines Ltd ZCCM.PA.
"The possibility of inviting other companies to join ZCI and Falconbridge in the consortium will be considered in due course," ZCI said.
Australian-based Western Mining Corp pulled out of the consortium last July.
The unidentified ore resource at the Konkola Deep mine contains 340 million tonnes at 3.8 percent copper content.
Zambia sees the $600 million development f the Konkola Deep mine as crucial to its mining industry which has been hard hit by declining copper output and depressed pribes on the world market.

The project envisages mining the ore body to a depth of around 1,740 metres to produce around six million tonnes of ore a year. Planned output would be around 180,000 tonnes of finished copper a year.
